hints: Focus on what happens to the electrons in the C=O double bond when the CN- nucleophile attacks the carbonyl carbon.
Remember the carbonyl oxygen is very electronegative, so it ends up with the pi electrons as a negatively charged alkoxide ion with CN now bonded through carbon.
Consider how that strongly basic O- ion is protonated by HCN, think about where the lone pair arrow starts and where the H-CN bond electrons must go to reform CN-.
walkthrough:
**Attack of cyanide on ethanal**

The CN- ion is a nucleophile and attacks the slightly positive carbonyl carbon of $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. The pi electrons of the $\text{C=O}$ move fully onto oxygen.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)O}^-$$

**Identify the intermediate ion**

Because oxygen gains both pi electrons, it becomes $\text{O}^-$ with three lone pairs, not $\text{O}^+$. The new bond is $\text{C-C}$ between the carbonyl carbon and the carbon of CN, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)-O}^-$.

**Protonation to form the cyanohydrin**

The alkoxide $\text{O}^-$ is a strong base and removes $\text{H}^+$ from a molecule of $\text{HCN}$. The correct curly arrows are a lone pair on $\text{O}^-$ to the $\text{H}$ of $\text{H-CN}$, and the $\text{H-CN}$ bond to the $\text{CN}$ to regenerate $\text{CN}^-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)O}^- + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(CN)OH} + \text{CN}^-$$

**Select the matching diagram**

Only the diagram showing a negatively charged oxygen, CN bonded via C, an arrow from $\text{O}^-$ to H, and an arrow from the H-CN bond onto CN matches this logic.

options.A: Incorrect. It shows oxygen as O+ which is impossible here. The C=O pi electrons move onto oxygen during nucleophilic attack, so oxygen must become O-, not O+. It also shows the wrong direction of electron flow for protonation.
options.B: Incorrect. The intermediate with O- and C-CN is correct, but the curly arrows for the next step are wrong. The protonation requires the O- lone pair to attack H and the H-CN bond to break to give CN-, which is not shown correctly here.
options.C: Incorrect. Like A, it shows oxygen as O+ instead of O-. Attack by negative CN- and movement of the pi electrons onto oxygen can only give a negative alkoxide ion. The charge alone rules this out.
options.D: Correct. The CN group is bonded through carbon to the former carbonyl carbon, and oxygen correctly carries a negative charge with lone pairs. The next step arrows are correct: lone pair on O- to H of HCN to form O-H, and H-CN bond electrons onto CN to reform the CN- catalyst and give the cyanohydrin CH3CH(CN)OH.
